| Dimension | Assessment |

| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Low-Medium |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Medium-High |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Affective computing — emotion recognition (facial, speech, physiological), affect generation, sentiment analysis, multimodal emotion, emotion-aware HCI |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **affective computing contribution**. Pure HCI without affect redirected.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Pure HCI redirected to TOCHI; pure psychology emotion research redirected to APA emotion venues.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Pure HCI without affect component
- AI use without disclosure per IEEE policy
- No benchmarking against existing affective computing methods

### Soft Tax

Low for affective computing tradition.

### Best Suited For

- Facial / speech / physiological emotion recognition
- Sentiment analysis advances
- Multimodal emotion integration
- Emotion-aware HCI systems
- Affective computing meta-analyses

### Not Recommended For

- Pure HCI without affect (consider TOCHI)
- Pure psychology emotion research
- Pure ML without affect application

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [IEEE Transactions on Human-Machine Systems](./ieee-transactions-on-human-machine-systems.md) | IEEE peer |
| 2 | [IEEE Access](./ieee-access.md) | IEEE OA mega-journal |
| 3 | [ACII conference proceedings](../conferences/hci/acii.md) | Affective computing conference venue |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a general AI venue as "too affect-specialized," IEEE TAC is the IEEE ACII-affiliated home.
